name: Dynamic Particle Isosurface Meshing
definition: A method for constructing isosurface triangulations of sampled, volumetric, three-dimensional scalar fields by using a system of dynamic particles to optimally sample an implicit function, ensuring the particles' relative positions produce a topologically correct Delaunay triangulation via global placement of triangle vertices.
summary: Dynamic Particle Isosurface Meshing constructs topologically correct isosurface triangulations via global particle placement, avoiding the self-intersection issues of advancing front methods.
